description: Current flagship smartphone: Bosch BMI260-class IMU, BMP390-class barometer, single-frequency GNSS.

noise_density.source: Bosch BMI260 product page (smartphone IMU): https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/products/motion-sensors/imus/bmi260/ — noise density 160 µg/√Hz

initial_bias_max.source: Bosch BMI260 product page (smartphone IMU): https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/products/motion-sensors/imus/bmi260/ — zero-g offset ±20 mg

bias_random_walk.source: Derived (A14): BMI260 TCO ±0.25 mg/K × 2 K over 180 s, spread as a random walk

scale_error_max.source: Bosch BMI260 product page (smartphone IMU): https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/products/motion-sensors/imus/bmi260/ — sensitivity error ±0.4%

noise_density.source: Bosch BMI260 product page (smartphone IMU): https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/products/motion-sensors/imus/bmi260/ — noise density 0.008 dps/√Hz

initial_bias_max.source: Bosch BMI260 product page (smartphone IMU): https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/products/motion-sensors/imus/bmi260/ — zero-rate offset ±0.5 dps

bias_random_walk.source: Derived (A14): BMI260 TCO ±0.02 dps/K × 2 K over 180 s, spread as a random walk

scale_error_max.source: Bosch BMI260 product page (smartphone IMU): https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/products/motion-sensors/imus/bmi260/ — sensitivity error ±0.4% (with CRT)

noise_std.source: Bosch BMP390: relative accuracy ±3 Pa, temperature coefficient ±0.6 Pa/K (datasheet BST-BMP390-DS002); ~0.1 m altitude noise floor (Adafruit BMP390 product page) — 0.1 m ≈ 1.2 Pa

drift_random_walk.source: Derived (A14): BMP390 ±0.6 Pa/K × 2 K over 180 s, spread as a random walk

position_std.source: GPS.gov accuracy page: smartphones typically within a 4.9 m radius (95%) under open sky; ≈2 m 1σ per horizontal axis

position_corr_time.source: Assumption A15: GNSS position error is time-correlated (multipath, atmosphere), first-order Gauss–Markov

speed_std.source: Assumption A15: Doppler-derived speed noise of a smartphone receiver in open sky

noise_std.source: Assumption A15: typical smartphone magnetometer noise; used only to show the tunnel disturbance
